title: Self-Host: Large file resumable upload always uses port 8000
body: # Bug report ## Describe the bug I am self-hosting Supabase and have modified the following configuration (environment variables) for my setup: KONG_HTTP_PORT=8089 SITE_URL=https://myhost:44307 API_EXTERNAL_URL=https://myhost:44307 SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL=https://myhost:44307 Small file uploads to Supabase Storage correctly use the external URL and port, e.g.: https://myhost:44307/storage/v1/upload/resumable However, large files that require resumable/multipart uploads always generate URLs pointing to http://myhost:8000/storage/v1//upload/resumable/dHJhaW5p..., ignoring the external port configuration. ## Expected behavior The generated resumable upload URL for large files should use the same external URL and port as small file uploads (https://myhost:44307/storage/v1/upload/resumable/...). ## Screenshots ## System information - OS: Windows - image: supabase/studio:2025.11.10-sha-5291fe3 - image: kong:2.8.1 - image: supabase/storage-api:v1.29.0

comments.author: BenIsenstein
comments.body: Hi, I've discovered this as well. The hardcoded port 8000 seems to be one issue, but the resumable upload over 6MB also constructs an `http` url strangely. This works in local dev over http, but not in a production environment behind a reverse proxy that expects `https`. I created a working example here that anyone can test to confirm the bug: https://supabasebugtus.freedynamicdns.net/ This is the latest version of the self-hosting example, running on a Linode machine, behind Caddy as a reverse proxy. Visit the url. Log into the Supabase Studio with the following username and password: user -> `supabase` pass -> `password` Visit the Storage panel in the UI. Upload a file under 6MB and note that it works. Upload a file over 6MB and note that it attempts to make the upload request to an `http` url, which is met with a `blocked:mixed-content` error in the network pane due to protocol mismatch.

comments.author: singh-inder
comments.body:
> As far as I can tell, it is indeed some logic in the Studio source code that builds the errant url. Trying to narrow down on this this afternoon.

Hi @BenIsenstein, its not an issue with studio. studio makes a request to storage service and storage service returns the url to upload chunk to.

As you've setup a proxy in front of kong, your request flow looks like this `user -> caddy -> kong -> storage`. 
The easiest solution is to directly proxy to storage service. You can add this block in your caddyfile (I'm assuming storage service is in the same network as caddy otherwise modify upstream storage url)

```caddyfile
handle_path /storage/v1/* {
	reverse_proxy storage:5000 {
		# you need to add cors headers. example snippet: https://github.com/singh-inder/supabase-automated-self-host/blob/main/docker/volumes/caddy/snippets/cors.conf
		import cors *
		#Make sure env var REQUEST_ALLOW_X_FORWARDED_PATH: "true" is set in storage service
		header_up X-Forwarded-Prefix /storage/v1
	}
}
```
This way your request flow will look like this: `user -> caddy -> storage`
Before you test again make sure to clear browser's local storage or try in private window.

If for some reason you want request to pass through kong, that can be done as well but requires some additional config.

comments.author: aantti
comments.body:
@Ryanznoco re:
> 44307 is a reverse proxy port that forwards 8089 to HTTPS with my domain name. Both large and small file uploads are accessed from the browser via `https://myhost:44307/`. However, the API endpoint used for large file uploads is `http://myhost:8000/storage/api/upload`, it is wrong, while small file uploads use `https://myhost:44307/storage/api/upload`, it is correct.

So it's an additional proxy in front of Kong, accepting external connections on port 44307, Kong behind the proxy exposed on port 8089 (but still port 8000 inside the container)?

What's happening here is that when passing the request to Storage, Kong sets `X-Forwarded-Port` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` headers with its _internal_ (inside the container) values. Storage builds the `location` header in its response to larger-than-6-MB uploads from these headers (if `REQUEST_ALLOW_X_FORWARDED_PATH` is set), and it becomes a wrong URL. There's a workaround for that, but it will require:
  1. Making sure your proxy sends `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Port` (usually requires manual config)
  2. Adding `KONG_TRUSTED_IPS` with your proxy's IP (so Kong trusts the forwarded headers)

However, a solution suggested by @singh-inder where you'd proxy to Storage directly, bypassing Kong - is probably way more straightforward.

comments.author: singh-inder
comments.body: @BenIsenstein This is not a bug. Storage service uses the headers it receives to construct the url for chunks. Kong passes `x-forwarded-port` ,`x-forwarded-prefix` and `x-forwarded-proto` to storage service. The `x-forwarded-port` header is set to the port kong is listening on internally (8000) and the x-forwarded-proto is http, this is why you see this url.

Smaller files work because those are uploaded in one go. This issue only arises when studio has to upload chunks of file. Because for these chunks it has to use the url returned by storage service.

If you don't want to proxy directly to storage, then you can use the method @aantti mentioned of adding caddy's ip in kong's trusted ips and then kong will automatically forward the headers it receives

comments.author: singh-inder
comments.body:
Clear the browser's local storage, open devtools network tab and try to upload a file > 6mb 
You will see that first a successful POST request is made. Check the response headers of this request and you will find a location header. This is the url studio makes PATCH requests to upload file chunks.

comments.author: gauravjain-code
comments.body: I have analysed codebase as well as the discussion for this issue now I am trying to summarize the whole situation which has been discussed so far around this issue and trying to clarify the things by connecting them so that anyone can understand and contribute. ### Hope this will clarify the whole situation: ### Root Cause - The Storage service builds the resumable upload URL for files > ~6MB from X-Forwarded headers. - Because Kong sits behind your HTTPS reverse proxy and doesn’t trust it, Kong forwards internal values to Storage: - x-forwarded-proto = http - x-forwarded-port = 8000 - Storage therefore returns a Location header with http://myhost:8000/... for the chunk endpoints. - The browser then attempts to PATCH that insecure URL, leading to mixed-content errors and failed uploads. ### Here is the fix which we can do: Keep Kong in the path and make it trust your reverse proxy Ensure your reverse proxy sets: X-Forwarded-Proto: https X-Forwarded-Port: 44307 (or 443 if you present 443 externally) In Kong: Set KONG_TRUSTED_IPS to include your reverse proxy’s IP(s) With trusted IPs, Kong will preserve the incoming X-Forwarded-* headers rather than substituting internal values.

comments.author: gauravjain-code
comments.body: Thanks for the screenshot — it actually explains what’s going on. When you open http://ip:8089/ directly, there’s no reverse proxy in front of Kong. In that case, Kong uses its own internal settings to build the “Location” for big (resumable) uploads. Kong’s internal port is 8000, so it tells Storage to return a Location like http://<host>:8000/.... That’s why your browser then tries to upload to port 8000, even though you started on 8089. You can make Kong “speak” the same port you use in the browser Configure Kong to listen on 8089 (e.g., KONG_PROXY_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8089) so the Location it builds uses 8089. See this diagram for fix

comments.author: allato
comments.body:
I was experiencing the same problem with resumable uploads. I was able to resolve it by modifying the TUS_URL_PATH environment variable in the storage service. Specifically, I changed it from:
`TUS_URL_PATH: /storage/v1/upload/resumable`
to:
`TUS_URL_PATH: /upload/resumable`
After this change, the uploads correctly used the proxied path, and everything works as expected behind my reverse proxy.

I think you might have mixed it up, though? (If changing, should be `TUS_URL_PATH: /storage/v1/upload/resumable`)

Again, do not use both `REQUEST_ALLOW_X_FORWARDED_PATH` and `TUS_URL_PATH` simultaneously in `docker-compose.yml`.

@Marchccc If there's no proxy on top of Kong → I believe you could add `KONG_PORT_MAPS: "8001:8000"` after the `environment` here:

https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/0e861a24fc91bcfa9244555e97db6e9e73023eea/docker/docker-compose.yml#L76-L77

```
    environment:
      KONG_PORT_MAPS: "8001:8000"
      KONG_DATABASE: "off"
```

comments.author: aantti
comments.body:
Ftr, see PRs [storage#900](https://github.com/supabase/storage/pull/900), and [storage#914](https://github.com/supabase/storage/pull/914):

- a new env var was added to Storage - `STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL`
- `STORAGE_PUBLIC_URL` was also [added to](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/26b3db830215b2e80c657aaa33b9d75d366945f0/docker/docker-compose.yml#L361) `docker-compose.yml` (via PR #43826)
- the new env var just basically tells Storage what external URL to use for TUS (by default it's the value of `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` from `.env`)
